message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Physical & Chemical Properties**

| Property | Value / Description | Notes |
|----------|---------------------|-------|
| **Atomic number** | 1 | Only one proton in the nucleus. |
| **Atomic mass** | 1.00794 u (average) | Dominated by the most abundant isotope, protium (¹H). |
| **Isotopes** | ¹H (protium, 99.98 %), ²H (deuterium, 0.02 %), ³H (tritium, trace, radioactive). | Deuterium and tritium are used in nuclear fusion research. |
| **Electron configuration** | 1s¹ | One valence electron. |
| **Electronegativity (Pauling)** | 2.20 | Highest of all elements. |
| **First ionization energy** | 13.598 eV (1312 kJ mol⁻¹) | Highest among all elements. |
| **Electron affinity** | –0.754 eV (–72.8 kJ mol⁻¹) | Negative, meaning H⁻ formation is endothermic. |
| **Molecular form** | H₂ (diatomic) | Stable under normal conditions; forms a covalent bond. |
| **Boiling point** | –252.87 °C (20.28 K) | Extremely low; hydrogen is a gas at room temperature. |
| **Melting point** | –259.16 °C (14.01 K) | Solidifies only at cryogenic temperatures. |
| **Density** | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ at 0 °C, 1 atm | Lightest element; less dense than air. |
| **Specific heat (gas)** | 14.304 J g⁻¹ K⁻¹ (at 25 °C) | High specific heat relative to its mass. |
| **Molar volume (ideal gas)** | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ at 0 °C, 1 atm | Standard molar volume. |
| **Reactivity** | Highly reactive; forms hydrides with metals, acids, and many nonmetals. | Forms H₂O, H₂S, HF, etc. |
| **Flammability** | Extremely flammable; explosive in air (range 4–75 % H₂ in air). | Requires careful handling. |
| **Acidity/Basicity** | Acts as a weak acid (forming H⁺) or base (forming H⁻) depending on context. | In aqueous solution, H⁺ is solvated as H₃O⁺. |
| **Bond dissociation energy (H–H)** | 436 kJ mol⁻¹ | Energy required to break the H₂ bond. |
| **Spectral lines** | Lyman, Balmer, Paschen series (UV, visible, IR). | Fundamental for astrophysical spectroscopy. |
| **Magnetic moment** | 2.792847 µB (for proton) | Proton’s magnetic moment; important in NMR. |
| **Fusion potential** | D–T fusion releases ~17.6 MeV per reaction. | Basis for experimental fusion reactors. |

### Quick Takeaways

- **Lightest element**: Only one proton and one electron; extremely low density.
- **Highly reactive**: Forms a wide variety of compounds; essential in organic chemistry and biochemistry.
- **Energy carrier**: Used in fuel cells (H₂ + O₂ → H₂O) and as a clean fuel source.
- **Astrophysical importance**: The most abundant element in the universe; its spectral lines are key to stellar observations.
- **Nuclear science**: Deuterium and tritium isotopes are central to fusion research.

Feel free to ask if you’d like deeper details on any specific property or application!
